chunks: And Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal narrated from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Zurara, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who marries a female slave (concubine). He said, 'If he is compelled by need, there is no objection.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no objection / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to marry his own female slave in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the permissibility of marrying one’s own female slave (milk al-yamin) under the condition of necessity (idtirar). This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that the prohibition is lifted to prevent illicit sexual relations when a man lacks the means to marry a free woman, emphasizing the functional role of slavery in classical family law.
